A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the APE proof-engineering project, retaining Mathlib commit-derived tasks and compilation plus semantic verification. All 20 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v3, including figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison despite the substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original seven-model experiments, patch-repair evaluations, structural and semantic failure analyses, and infrastructure measurements in Sections 4–5.

after.justification: v3 reports original model and scaffold evaluations, tool ablations, expert validation of 64 judged solutions, and infrastructure measurements in Section 6, with execution and disagreement examples in Appendices A–B.

M1.justification: The described workflow changes from sampled unified-diff generation with DiffRepair to APE-Harness task contracts and an interactive APE-Agent scaffold. v3 adds version-scoped retrieval, integrated editing and compilation, nested judgment tasks, and agent-based instruction synthesis. Compilation plus semantic verification and content-addressable storage remain, but these additions substantially change execution.

E1.justification: Mathlib file-edit tasks remain, while v3 adds actual theorem-proving evaluations on miniF2F and miniCTX; v1 used these benchmarks only for descriptive context/token comparisons. v3 also introduces an expert-annotated solution set for evaluating semantic judgment. Its repository-scale framing does not establish a new evaluated multi-file editing task.

E2.justification: v1 Table 2 compares o3-mini, Claude Sonnet 3.7 with and without thinking, DeepSeek R1/V3, GPT-4o, and Doubao 1.5 Pro. v3 replaces this lineup with GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, and Gemini 3 Flash, and additionally evaluates Claude Code and Codex CLI against APE-Agent on corresponding APE-Bench tasks.

E3.justification: v1's zero-shot patch-generation and pass@16 evaluation becomes an interactive evaluation with a $3 budget, 100-turn limit, and top-5 retrieval. The historical Mathlib setup is replaced by 100 tasks from 67 commits dated January 6–12, 2026. v3 also adds a 64-solution expert-validation protocol reporting dimension-specific accuracy and false-positive/negative counts.

E4.justification: v1's patch-size, difficulty, mathematical-domain, patch-length, repairability, and semantic-error analyses are largely removed. v3 adds file/shell/retrieval ablations, scaffold tool-use analysis, expert judge validation, a complete agent walkthrough, and three judge-disagreement case studies. These investigate substantially different failure mechanisms and implementation choices.

E5.justification: Judgment aggregation changes from four independent Claude samples to three GPT-5.2 judgments. v1 explicitly specifies 20 candidate samples per task; v3 provides no corresponding repeated-agent-run count. Neither reports random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. This changes sampling disclosure and aggregation without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The principal results are replaced: v1 Table 2 reports o3-mini leading at 33.58% semantic pass@16, whereas v3 Figure 3 reports APE-Agent success rates of 47% for Gemini 3 Flash, 27% for GPT-5.2, and 24% for Gemini 3 Pro. These are different models, tasks, and protocols, not a same-setting improvement. New findings include 90.6% overall judge agreement and 44–47% tool-ablation success.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theorem-and-proof analysis of the proposed framework. v3's task contracts and historical Lean proof examples describe procedures and benchmark content rather than new theoretical results. Removal of v1's standard pass@k estimator formula is an evaluation-documentation change.

C1.justification: v1 presents a file-level benchmark and Eleanstic, with autonomous workflows positioned as future stages. v3 claims a complete repository-scale evaluation infrastructure centered on task contracts, APE-Agent, scaffold interchangeability, and execution across different task types. Expert judge validation and a claimed contamination-free benchmark instantiation become explicit contributions.

C2.justification: v1 interprets failures through edit scale, omissions, and inadequate structural planning. v3 instead emphasizes cost-efficiency, scaffold overhead, and a claimed reasoning bottleneck inferred from similar tool-ablation results. Sections 6.3 and Appendix B newly discuss judge scope-control failures, destructive edits, and inconsistent tolerance of benign refactoring.

D1.justification: v3 supplies an explicit repository link and declares code/data released, adds workspace-permission and retrieval details, and documents a task's commit, toolchain, execution time, token usage, and cost. v1's snapshot encoding and DiffRepair implementation descriptions disappear. Reproducibility remains imperfect: v3 Appendix A.1 specifies Lean 4.27.0-rc1, while A.4 names Lean 4.3.0 for the same example.

R1.justification: Related work shifts from a broad history of theorem-proving models and benchmarks toward repository-scale engineering and agent infrastructure. v3 adds positioning around REPLICA, FATE, Seed-Prover, Gauss, Aristotle, LangGraph, and SWE-agent, while removing substantial discussion of systems such as HOList, GamePad, FIMO, and LEGO-Prover. miniCTX remains the same cited work despite bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around the infrastructure contribution. Task formulation and harness design precede benchmark construction, and experiments are reorganized around efficiency, judging, scaffolds, and tools. The DiffRepair appendix is replaced by a walkthrough and semantic-validation cases; the title and author list also change.

P2.justification: v3 partly reuses the benchmark-comparison illustration within a redesigned framework overview, but removes the staged roadmap and most dataset and diagnostic graphics. It adds a boxed task example, paired cost/turn plots across six experiment groups, a stacked tool-use chart, and new contract, judge-accuracy, and ablation tables. This substantially changes the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful agent comparisons, tool ablations, and expert judge validation that v1 lacked, but removes extensive stratified diagnostics. Its central validation evidence remains difficult to reconcile: Section 6.3 says all 64 evaluated solutions compiled, while Appendix B.1 presents a non-compiling judge-failure example without clarifying its relationship to that sample. Appendix A also reports conflicting toolchains. These unresolved issues prevent a reliable net-quality judgment despite the substantive additions.
